summary.title: The Manager FAQ
summary.one_liner: A Q&A for engineers new to business settings on how to work with managers, covering when management helps, common friction points, and how to handle them.
keywords: manager wants me to look busy
takeaways: Management is a form of work; a good manager can run interference and raise team productivity, while a poor fit can get in the way of creative or fundamental engineering work.
Assume your manager is broadly aware of requirements and respect their position in the hierarchy, even when their habits seem odd.
Design progress is hard to estimate, so express work state through whiteboards and written summaries to show progress.
Address complaints by talking to the manager directly and explaining reasoning rather than retaliating or nagging.
Expect the manager to need estimates and predictable schedules for business reasons, and give estimates with stated uncertainty.
summary.summary: This is a classic FAQ by Peter Seebach, written for hackers entering the business world, first published in 2000-2001 (revision 0.01). It is organized as numbered questions such as whether a manager is useful, how to handle a manager who wants you to look busy, or how to give estimates for design work that is hard to measure. Each answer is a short, opinionated explanation of the manager's likely reasons, followed by practical suggestions for the engineer. The author states an explicit bias toward engineers, and the page is informal and dated in places.
